lead.headline: MeitY releases DEPA handbook so institutions can share data for AI training without handing it over
signal: If institutions adopt it, AI teams in India could get access to sensitive data (health, finance) that is currently locked away, without moving it.
The handbook is a framework, not a mandate. Uptake depends on whether data holders trust the contracts and technical controls.
lead.hook: MeitY has ==launched a handbook on DEPA (Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture) for AI training==, a framework that lets institutions pool data for models while keeping control of it.
points: IT Secretary S Krishnan unveiled the handbook at a Bengaluru roundtable. It was developed with the iSPIRT Foundation, per an official release issued Saturday.
The mechanism: the model travels to the data, not the reverse, according to Principal Scientific Adviser Ajay Kumar Sood. Raw data stays with its owner.
The framework combines contractual permissions, controlled computing environments and privacy-enhancing safeguards. Data provenance traces the origin, permissions and use of data through training.
It targets the blockers to sharing: privacy, confidentiality, intellectual property and institutional control. Sood says it enables multi-party and cross-border collaboration.
Krishnan said MeitY is committed to taking the framework forward. The release gave no timeline, pilots or named participants.
lead.key_stat: Model goes to the data · DEPA handbook
lead.editors_read: Data, not compute, is often the binding constraint for Indian AI, and holders refuse to share because they lose control once data leaves. DEPA tries to change that by making permission and traceability technical. If a few large data holders sign on, Indian startups get a differentiated training-data source; if not, this stays a document. Watch for named pilots, which the release did not give.

frontpage.headline: OpenAI falls short in fundraising: ==$11B secured against== a $30B target
signal: Capital is scarce relative to AI spending needs: OpenAI and Anthropic both burn cash, and even Meta, Google and Amazon are now cash-negative.
If Anthropic's IPO prices well, it takes funding share from OpenAI at the moment OpenAI's private round is weakest.
frontpage.hook: OpenAI has secured about $11 billion of its $30 billion target, at a $1.25 trillion valuation versus the $1.4 trillion it sought, the Wall Street Journal reports.
points: OpenAI now __aims to raise up to $20 billion from family__ offices and wealthy individuals, per reports. The reported cause is fading interest from big investors during a tech sell-off after weak results from Google, Amazon and Intel.
It is also reportedly planning an IPO early next year.
Rival Anthropic is looking to list in November at $1.5-2 trillion, possibly raising up to $100 billion. That would exceed SpaceX's record $85.7 billion IPO in June.
Meta sold $37.5 billion of stock last week and plans $60 billion more in early 2027. Microsoft sold $25 billion of bonds. Amazon has raised about $130 billion of long-term debt over the past year.
The Nasdaq-100 fell 6.65% in October. Neoclouds (AI compute rental firms) CoreWeave and Nebius each lost over a third of their value.
frontpage.editors_read: The cheque sizes show investors can still fund one frontier lab, but not all of them plus hyperscaler bond issuance at once. OpenAI's pivot to wealthy individuals signals that institutional demand is limited at this price. The price cuts mentioned in the piece suggest it is defending share while its funding is weaker, which could pressure margins industry-wide.

frontpage.headline: Indian deeptech funding nearly tripled in Q3, but to fewer companies, as VCs face criticism
signal: Headline growth overstates access: more money to fewer, validated companies means first-time founders with unproven technology may still struggle.
For 2025, deeptech raised about $500M across 87 deals, below fintech's $2.5B. If the Q3 pace holds, it closes much of that gap.
frontpage.hook: Indian deeptech ==raised $290M in Q3== 2026, up 176% year on year, yet across 28 deals versus 29 a year earlier, per Inc42 DataLabs.
points: Pixxel's $100M round alone was about a third of the quarter's deeptech capital. Bengaluru took around 65% of the funding.

Journalist Ashlee Vance asked why Indian VCs avoid risk after meeting 15 companies. Founders cite demands for revenue before the technology is validated, slow diligence and reliance on IIT/IIM pedigree.
Dognosis founder Akash Kulgod, after pitching about 80 investors (around 65% US-based), says US investors decide faster while some Indian ones keep talks going and then ask for traction.

Investors counter with successes: Skyroot reached orbit in July, and Antler says it was first institutional backer of 10 deeptech ventures since 2022. Airbound's $37M Series A was led by US-based Greenoaks.
Unacademy's Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini are raising a ₹700 Cr fund, Longshot Capital, for AI, manufacturing, robotics, spacetech and defence.
frontpage.editors_read: The concentration (one round is a third of the total) means Q3 reflects a few big bets, not broad risk appetite. The test is whether early-stage deal counts rise. New founder-run funds like Longshot are a plausible fix because operators can judge technical risk themselves.

frontpage.headline: Meta reportedly built a humanoid robot prototype with Chinese startup Fourier
signal: A US platform partnering with a Chinese hardware maker is notable given tension between the two countries; scrutiny is possible if the report holds.
frontpage.hook: Meta has built a prototype humanoid robot with Chinese robotics startup Fourier, in about three months, and is working on a second version, The Information reported Saturday.
points: The report cites people familiar with the initiative; the coverage lines here do not state further details of the design.
It comes as Meta steps up efforts to develop robots, with one outlet linking the work to Llama-powered AI and an acquisition called ARI.
Meta has not confirmed the report in the coverage provided (summary from limited source text).

frontpage.headline: India halts Sun Pharma's eye-drop production at its Assam plant after quality lapses
signal: The direct revenue hit looks small, but a repeat of sterile-plant problems could slow Sun's stated sterile-products growth plan.
frontpage.hook: Regulators ordered Sun Pharma to stop all ophthalmic production at its Assam plant, after a recall of 332 batches of eye-drop products.
points: A joint central-state inspection found lapses in the quality management system. A show-cause notice went out on August 10; regulators then judged the reply unsatisfactory and halted manufacture, sale and distribution.
Production stays stopped until regulators accept the company's compliance report, now under review. Sun says it voluntarily paused and put remedial measures in place.

The recalled brands include Lotepred, Nepalact and Brinzotim. Experts say the batches could be hundreds of thousands of bottles. Sun described the recall to stockists as precautionary and did not publicly disclose it.
In June the All India Ophthalmological Society warned that certain Predmet batches appeared contaminated.
Ophthalmology is about 3% of Sun's domestic revenue. The site was meant to be a major sterile-products hub. The US FDA halted shipments from its Halol plant last year.

frontpage.headline: India-Bangladesh Ganga water treaty may lapse on December 12 without renewal
signal: If the visit does not happen before December 12, the treaty lapses just before the lean season, leaving water sharing without a legal framework.
frontpage.hook: The 30-year-old Ganga water treaty expires on December 12, and India is unlikely to renew it automatically without a visit from Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman, sources say.
points: The 1996 treaty governs lean-season sharing (January 1-May 31) of Ganges water, controlled at Farakka Barrage, about 20 km upstream of Bangladesh. Shorter tenure and other changes are being considered.
Terms: 50:50 sharing when flow is above 70,000 cusecs; below that, Bangladesh gets a fixed 35,000 cusecs, alternating in three 10-day periods March 11-May 10.
In India, Bihar's chief minister wants state interests protected, citing rising demand from Bihar to West Bengal, industry and thermal plants. Siltation near Farakka is also raised.
Bangladesh's ruling BNP wants the 1977 'minimum guarantee' (80% of scheduled allocation) restored and calls the 1996 template inadequate for its farmers.
Rahman's visit has been planned at least four times and derailed, per the report, amid Hasina extradition disputes and pressure from Jamaat-e-Islami.

frontpage.headline: India needs 7.6x more energy storage by FY32, CareEdge says
signal: Capacity without storage and grid does not become reliable supply. If the plan holds, batteries and transmission are the big investment pools ahead.
frontpage.hook: India must add ==357.4 GWh of energy storage== over six years: capacity is about 54 GWh as of June 2026 against 411.4 GWh needed by FY32.
points: The FY32 need under the CEA's National Electricity Plan splits into 236.22 GWh of batteries and 175.18 GWh of pumped storage.
Investment estimated at ₹3.49 lakh crore for batteries and ₹1.29 lakh crore for pumped storage, about ₹4.78 lakh crore combined.
Non-fossil sources were 54.18% of installed capacity in June 2026, but coal still supplies most actual generation.
Solar and wind output is intermittent, so storage is needed to move power to peak demand; the report calls transmission a major gap.
India targets 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.

stories.headline: OpenAI's round reportedly led by UAE investors after target cut
signal: Gulf capital is filling the gap that US institutions left.
stories.hook: The FT reports OpenAI cut its funding target to $20 billion, with a ==first close expected to be== lower, led by UAE investors.
points: The WSJ says $11 billion is secured so far and some large investors were 'tepid'.
A later retail offering to wealthy individuals __could bring the total to $20 billion__.
Earlier reports had it raising $30 billion at $1.4 trillion, then at $1.25 trillion, ahead of an IPO.
TechCrunch links the trouble partly to a tech sell-off over AI infrastructure spending.

stories.headline: Anthropic extends text watermark to four more Claude models, with a loophole on two
signal: Anyone relying on the watermark for compliance must keep default settings.
stories.hook: Anthropic is watermarking four more Claude models, but on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 users can avoid it by changing one sampling setting.
points: Covered: Claude Mythos 5, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6. Newer models like Opus 5.5 already carry it.
On the two 4.6 models the mark applies only when temperature, top_p and top_k are at defaults; changing any one evades it.
Anthropic cites the EU AI Act's December deadline. The mark is a SynthID-style variant, cannot be turned off and contains no user data.
OpenAI's textGrain activates by default only for EU ChatGPT and Codex users; API users can toggle it, and it ships disabled.

stories.headline: DeepMind and WRI release ForTy, a global forest-type map for EU deforestation rules
signal: Useful as a screening layer, not proof for compliance given the plantation error rates.
stories.hook: Google DeepMind and WRI built ForTy, a 10-metre global map of 2020 land into six classes, correct in 90.2% of 8,190 expert-checked sites.
points: It matters because the EU deforestation regulation bans goods linked to forest cleared after December 31, 2020, so firms need a 2020 baseline.
It beats European Commission maps: 90.9% versus 87.8% on forest types.
Weakness: it finds only about half of tree crops and planted forests and 60% of plantations; those are the boundaries the EUDR cares about.
The map overestimates Asian primary forest by about 200 million hectares and misses about 94 million hectares in Africa.
Data is free under CC BY 4.0, including in Google Earth Engine.

stories.headline: Judge lets NAACP Clean Air Act suit over xAI's Memphis turbines proceed
signal: Permit risk for on-site gas power is now a real cost for data center builders.
stories.hook: A federal judge denied xAI's motion to dismiss the NAACP suit alleging at least 35 turbines at its Colossus data center ran without air permits.
points: xAI argued the turbines are mobile and exempt, and that plaintiffs lacked standing. The judge rejected both and the constitutional challenge to citizen suits.
A similar Department of Justice motion to dismiss was denied earlier this month.
New York recently passed a moratorium on new data centers; Amazon and Microsoft promised to stop using NDAs with government agencies.

also.line: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman met Samsung's top executives in South Korea on Saturday to deepen cooperation on memory chips and AI infrastructure as shortages intensify.
Creatives in PM Albanese's Sydney seat oppose a proposal letting AI firms train on Australian works by default; draft laws are expected by year-end, parliament in 2027.

stories.headline: CapGrid ==raises ₹50== Cr to move into precision components, drones and data centres
signal: The target implies growth well above FY26's 14%.
stories.hook: CapGrid raised ₹50 Cr (about $5.2M) at a ₹430 Cr valuation, led by Hero Enterprise Venture Partners.
points: It owns no factories; its platform uses third-party manufacturers, which it says run at about 60% capacity, pooling OEM orders.
FY26 operating revenue grew about 14% to ₹240 Cr; target for FY27 is ₹350 Cr. Run rate is ₹360-370 Cr.
Funds partly go to R&D in higher-end engineered components.
Inc42 notes no margin or working-capital disclosures, so better returns from complex orders are unclear.

also.line: Yulu narrowed its FY26 loss 23% to Rs 96.6 crore as revenue rose 18.6% to Rs 281 crore from Rs 237 crore, with EV rentals the largest stream.

stories.headline: Pixxel sets up US subsidiary to chase government contracts
signal: US federal work diversifies revenue away from India's government.
stories.hook: Pixxel created Pixxel Federal in the US to sell earth-observation and satellite systems to American civilian, defence and intelligence agencies.
points: It builds on a NASA commercial smallsat data contract and an NRO Strategic Commercial Enhancements contract.
Allyson Jenkins, who has led US government business since January 2025, is CEO; an office near Washington, DC is planned.
Pixxel raised $100M Series C in September, led by Temasek and Seraphim; total funding is about $195M.
It is also building a 12-satellite public-private constellation under IN-SPACe.

also.line: DRDO showcased indigenous semiconductor technologies for radar, electronic warfare and missile systems (source unreachable — headline only).

stories.headline: Apple Intelligence reaches China in December, with Alibaba's Qwen
signal: China is Apple's second-largest market, so this removes a feature gap versus local rivals.
stories.hook: Apple will launch about 18 Apple Intelligence features in China with iOS 27.3 in December, using Alibaba's Qwen model, after a developer beta from November 4.
points: Regulators granted Apple the licence in July, alongside six other phone AI services including Samsung and Huawei.
Features include writing tools, live translation and visual intelligence; the latest Siri AI capabilities from September are excluded.
Qwen handles text, image generation and photo or document analysis via Siri.
No date was given for other Apple devices in China.

also.line: Cloudflare's post-quantum GeoKey Manager entered closed beta on October 23 using ML-KEM-768 plus X25519, replacing attribute-based encryption; general availability is planned for Q1 2027.

stories.headline: COP17 concludes: nature goals off track, finance fight deferred
signal: Funding gap against the $200bn-a-year 2030 goal stays unresolved.
stories.hook: At COP17 in Yerevan, countries' ==first global review said== the 2030 goal to reverse nature loss and meet 23 targets 'will not be achieved' unless action accelerates.
points: Developed countries missed the target of at least $20bn a year for nature by 2025; environmental funding is down 27% for 2026-30.
Countries want to widen who pays: nations may 'signal interest' to be listed as donors before COP18; no criteria were set.
A post-2030 finance mechanism is agreed under the COP, but whether it is a new fund is deferred to COP18.
COP18 will be in Quito, Ecuador, in 2028.

also.line: Tamil Nadu's solar generation hit an all-time high of 8,818 MW on Friday, the first time it has reached such a level in October, as monsoon rains paused.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing makes life sciences its next big business
signal: Pharma gives high-value use for premium models, but the payoff depends on drug approvals.
stories.hook: Anthropic's S-1 says nine of the 10 ==largest pharma companies spent== at least $100,000 with it in a recent year.
points: Pharma spend is expected to exceed $2 trillion in 2026; Claude is used in drug discovery.
Moves: Claude Science (beta, June), a molecular biology lab, a $400M stock purchase of Coefficient Bio, and Novartis CEO on the board.
Lilly has 50,000 employees with Claude access, over 85% active users.
No AI-designed drug has FDA approval.

stories.headline: India's pharma exports rise 4.9% to ==$16.14B in H1== FY27 as US shipments soften
signal: Growth is diversifying away from price-pressured US generics.
stories.hook: India's pharma exports reached $16.14 billion in April-September, up 4.9% from $15.38 billion.
points: Europe grew 9.66% to $3.29 billion (20.38% of exports); ASEAN rose 21.54%, Latin America 16.58%, Africa 6.48%.
US shipments moderated; Pharmexcil gave no figure.
Formulations (73.84%) grew 3.81%; bulk drugs and intermediates rose 12.07%.
Listed drugmakers absorb a 100-120 basis point margin hit from solvent and crude prices.

stories.headline: FBI blames North Korea for ==$6.3B Binance hack==
signal: Customers are made whole, but the loss is a heavy hit to Binance's reserves.
stories.hook: The FBI says North Korea's TraderTraitor group stole about $6.3 billion from Binance in the biggest crypto heist on record.
points: The same group was blamed for last year's $1.5 billion Bybit hack.
Hackers are converting funds mainly into Ethereum and are expected to launder them via DeFi and instant swaps.
Binance says it replaced 90% of stolen assets from its $1 billion SAFU fund, insurance fund and treasury, and will cover the rest.
Entry point was a compromised engineer laptop; withdrawals are due to reopen Sunday.

also.line: SEBI barred EKI Energy Services MD Manish Dabkara for 12 months and the company for two months over misrepresented financials and fund diversion; ex-CFO barred eight months.
also.source: Business News Today: Latest Business News, Finance News

stories.headline: Scotch bulk-import duty row tests the India-UK trade deal
signal: The outcome shows how strictly India reads tariff concessions.
stories.hook: India told liquor firms bulk Scotch imports do not get the cut from 150% to 75% duty, and the commerce ministry meets industry Monday.
points: About 80% of Scotch imported by volume arrives in bulk for domestic brands.
Diageo, Pernod Ricard and the Indian association CIABC (Radico Khaitan, Allied Blenders) object.
CIABC warns it would favour importing finished whisky over Make in India production.
It is the first major dispute under the deal, in force since July.

stories.headline: Jio Platforms lists in ==India's largest IPO and becomes its second== most valuable company
signal: Starlink entry would test its position.
stories.hook: Jio Platforms raised $3.2 billion in India's biggest IPO, and shares rose 21% on debut to a $131.5 billion valuation.
points: Jio has over 530 million customers; Meta and Google are shareholders.
Its 2016 launch cut average revenue per subscriber 42.8% by 2019; seven of 10 incumbents exited.
Jio, Airtel and Vodafone Idea control over 92% of the market.
Jio raised tariffs 12-25% in July 2024, but warns further rises may not lift revenue.

also.line: Gor hopes to take the US-India trade deal 'across the finish line' and hints at 'exciting outcomes' before the G20 (source unreachable — headline only).

stories.headline: What US midterms could mean for H-1B and green cards
signal: Expect more oversight, not quick reversal, even if Democrats win.
stories.hook: Market estimates put the odds of Democrats winning both US chambers at 63%, which could slow Republican H-1B tightening, an ICICI report says.
points: Pending bills include higher wage thresholds and stiffer H-1B fraud penalties; the SMARTER Act proposes a points-based green card system.
The President's veto limits change; Congress has already funded $70 billion for ICE and Border Patrol.
Key issues: wage requirements, compliance, green card eligibility and renewals.

opportunities.name: Top Business Schools Present: Application Tips (Virtual)
opportunities.summary: Admissions reps from ten MBA schools including Booth, Harvard, Stanford, Wharton and MIT Sloan share application tips. Online; link shared on registration.
